root_cause_criterion.criterion: Before `crc16_update_block_()` may call `FLAC__crc16_update_words32()`, it must establish `br->consumed_words > br->crc16_offset` so the helper sees a non-wrapping word count and an in-range starting pointer.
root_cause_criterion.description: The vulnerable original reaches the protected bulk-CRC call even though the required source guard is false at the root site (`consumed_words_now=1`, `crc16_offset_now=2`). The fixed original is guarded on the stock PoC, and the closest source-grounded witness `readcb2_size13_append8` executes the same protected call with the predicate true (`3 > 2`) and exits cleanly.

nodes.description: At the CRC helper sink, the vulnerable original enters the two-word loop body because the passed `len` still covers at least one `words[0]`/`words[1]` pair.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original assertion trace records `crc16_words32_sink.len_arg=4294967295` and `pair_width_words=2`, so the sink-side pair read executes.

nodes.description: At the vulnerable bulk CRC call, the wrapped word count presented to `FLAC__crc16_update_words32()` is larger than the whole bitreader buffer capacity, which is the concrete out-of-bounds precondition for the sink.
nodes.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `call_len_words=4294967295 > capacity_words=2048`.

nodes.description: The bitreader clear resets the live consumption counters to zero but leaves the saved CRC cursor ahead of them, creating the stale-state condition needed for the later wraparound.
nodes.evidence: The frozen traces record `clear_offset=2 > consumed_words_after_clear=0` at `FLAC__bitreader_clear()`.

edges.relation: The same stale `br->crc16_offset` compared at the missing root guard is the offset used to advance `br->buffer` for the bulk CRC call.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `crc16_bulk_guard.crc16_offset_now == crc16_words32_call.call_offset_words == 2`; the fixed witness preserves the same equality when the guarded call genuinely executes.

edges.relation: The wrapped bulk-call length is passed unchanged into the sink helper as its `len` argument, so the sink observes the same oversized count created at the root call site.
edges.evidence: The vulnerable original trace records `crc16_words32_call.call_len_words == crc16_words32_sink.len_arg == 4294967295`.

edges.relation: The stale `crc16_offset` preserved across `FLAC__bitreader_clear()` reaches the later bulk-CRC guard unchanged, which is why the wrapped subtraction is still computed against the pre-clear cursor.
edges.evidence: Both the vulnerable original and the fixed guarded original record `crc16_clear_state.clear_offset == crc16_bulk_guard.crc16_offset_now == 2`.

edges.relation: The CRC cursor snapshot taken by `FLAC__bitreader_reset_read_crc16()` is the same saved offset later observed at `FLAC__bitreader_clear()`, showing that the clear operates on a stale pre-clear CRC position.
